title: Improve based on real conversations
learningGoal: Track whether the journey helps clients take the next step.

items.title: Enquiry Form Submissions
items.description: Count how many forms were submitted each week.

items.title: First Emails Successfully Sent
items.description: Track delivery and identify any sending failures.

items.title: Replies and Bookings
items.description: Measure replies and appointment bookings attributable to those enquiries.

items.title: Unsubscribes and Complaints
items.description: Monitor unsubscribes, complaints, and duplicate follow-ups.

items.title: Common Questions
items.description: Identify questions that the first email could answer better.

items.title: Do Not Compare Raw Counts Alone
items.description: Do not compare raw booking counts without also considering the number and quality of enquiries.

items.title: Start with an Observation
items.description: Notice a pattern, make one small change, then check results.

items.title: Exercise for Coaches
items.description: If many people reply with questions but few book, what could you change about the email? Write one answer that helps the prospect before asking them to book.

keyPoint: Review weekly: form submissions, emails sent, replies, bookings, unsubscribes, and common questions. Do not compare raw booking counts without considering enquiry quality. Make one small change at a time.

actionSteps.title: Set up weekly tracking
actionSteps.description: Create a simple tracker for form submissions, emails sent, replies, bookings, and unsubscribes.

actionSteps.title: Review common questions
actionSteps.description: Look at replies and identify questions your first email could answer better.

actionSteps.title: Make one small improvement
actionSteps.description: Choose one change to test — a clearer subject line, a better booking link placement, or an added FAQ sentence.

quizzes.question: What should you review weekly to improve your follow-up journey?

options.option_text: Form submissions, emails sent, replies, bookings, unsubscribes, and common questions

quizzes.explanation: Review form submissions, first emails sent, replies and bookings, unsubscribes and complaints, and common questions. This gives a complete picture of how the journey is performing.

quizzes.question: Why should you not compare raw booking counts alone?

options.option_text: Because you must also consider the number and quality of enquiries
Because the workflow does not track bookings
Because booking counts are always inaccurate

quizzes.explanation: Raw booking counts without context can be misleading. A drop in bookings might reflect fewer or lower-quality enquiries, not a broken follow-up process. Always consider enquiry volume and quality.

quizzes.question: What is the recommended approach to improving the follow-up journey?

options.option_text: Redesign the entire workflow every week
Start with an observation, make one small change, then check results

quizzes.explanation: Start with an observation from your weekly review, make one small change, then check results. This controlled approach helps you understand what actually improves performance.
